question: Compared to flat mirrors, convex (rounded) mirrors give a wider view of the road behind, but also:

choices.A: Make vehicles seem closer than they really are
choices.B: Make vehicles seem farther away than they really are
choices.C: Cannot be legally used on a motorcycle
choices.D: Eliminate the need for a head check

explanation: Universal riding-safety fact taught in state manuals nationwide: convex mirrors widen the field of view but make following vehicles look farther away than they actually are, so riders must practice judging real distance with them.

question: Why is checking your mirrors alone not enough before changing lanes on a motorcycle?

choices.A: Mirrors are often broken on motorcycles
choices.B: State law prohibits relying on mirrors while moving
choices.C: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars, so a head check is also needed
choices.D: Mirrors only work correctly at night

explanation: Universal riding-safety fact taught in state manuals nationwide: motorcycles have blind spots just like cars, so a rider must turn their head and look before changing lanes, not rely on mirrors alone.
